explain.say: At home you can switch off the TV and the lamp stays on. The kettle can boil while the fridge hums. How? Your home is wired in parallel, which means each appliance has its own path, called a branch. Let us trace the paths.

explain.say: Look at the mains supply on the left. In many countries, like India and the UK, it gives about 230 volts. It feeds the fuse box, and from there the wire splits into branches. Can you count the branches?

explain.say: Three, yes! Now here is the key: each branch connects straight across the supply, so the TV, the kettle and the lamp each get the full 230 volts. Nothing is shared, so each one works at full power. Does the lamp get less voltage than the TV?

explain.say: No, the same! But the currents add up. If the kettle takes 13 amps, the TV 1 and the lamp a little, the main wire carries them all together. That is why the fuse box protects the main wire. What happens if you switch the TV off?

explain.say: Only that branch stops; the others carry on. Wonderful work! Wow fact: switching on more things in parallel actually lowers the total resistance, so more current flows from the supply. Challenge: count how many separate branches you can switch in your kitchen.

faq.q: Why do homes use parallel circuits?
faq.a: Each appliance gets the full mains voltage and can be switched on or off without affecting the others.
asks: Why are houses wired in parallel?

faq.q: What does the fuse box do?
faq.a: It holds fuses or circuit breakers that cut the power if too much current flows, protecting the wires from overheating.

faq.q: What voltage does each branch get?
faq.a: Every branch in parallel gets the same voltage as the supply, such as the full 230 volts of the mains.
asks: Is voltage the same in a parallel circuit?

faq.q: What happens if one appliance is switched off?
faq.a: Only its own branch is broken. Current still flows through all the other branches.
asks: What happens if one bulb breaks in parallel?

faq.q: How does current behave in a parallel circuit?
faq.a: The current splits between the branches and the branch currents add up to the total current from the supply.

facts: In a parallel circuit, every branch has the same potential difference as the supply.
The branch currents in a parallel circuit add up to the total supply current.

quiz.say: Two lamps are in parallel on a 12 V battery. Voltage across each lamp?
quiz.show: Two lamps are in parallel on a 12 V battery. Voltage across each lamp?
quiz.why: Each parallel branch connects straight across the supply, so each gets 12 volts.

wrong.0: Voltage is shared in series, not in parallel.
wrong.2: A branch cannot get more than the supply voltage.

quiz.say: Branch currents are 2 A, 3 A and 1 A. What is the total current?
quiz.show: Branch currents are 2 A, 3 A and 1 A. What is the total current?

wrong.0: That is just the biggest branch; the branches add up.
wrong.1: That is an average, not the total.
